title: Efficiency: GCM decrypt accumulates entire ciphertext in provider inbuf
description: wolfssl_aes_gcm.c — the decrypt path (wolfssl_aes_gcm_update) allocates an inbuf in the session context that grows to hold the entire ciphertext before any decryption occurs. This is architecturally correct (unauthenticated plaintext must not be released before tag verification), but it means a 1MB decrypt requires 1MB in the provider context PLUS 1MB in the framework outbuf — peak memory is 2x payload. At CRYPTO2DEV_MAX_PAYLOAD=1MB, a single GCM decrypt session can consume up to 2MB of kernel heap. In deployments with many concurrent decrypt sessions, this is real pressure. Document the 2x factor; consider whether a lower ceiling for AEAD decrypt is appropriate.
